subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` defaults be allowed to override later global `tools.exec.*` config changes for Discord and other channel sessions?
rationale: Current source and tests treat `/exec` as a durable session default, while the report asks to make administrator/global security config take precedence; that is a security-boundary and compatibility choice.

options.title: Global policy floor
options.body: Keep `/exec` as a session convenience only when it stays within the current global/admin policy, and add focused reset/migration/tests/docs for older persisted fields.

options.title: Keep durable session override
options.body: Accept the current behavior as intentional, document that existing sessions can retain `/exec` defaults until reset, and add operator-facing inspection or reset guidance.

options.title: Make `/exec` ephemeral
options.body: Stop persisting exec directives entirely so config changes win after restart, accepting a breaking change for users who expect durable session exec defaults.

recommendation.title: Global policy floor
recommendation.body: Keep `/exec` as a session convenience only when it stays within the current global/admin policy, and add focused reset/migration/tests/docs for older persisted fields.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person to the current directive/session implementation and adjacent docs/tests.
